key_insight: CareMirror reframes dementia care by making caregiver wellbeing a first-class part of the care ecosystem, not an afterthought. It connects caregivers and clinicians through longitudinal reflection and caregiver-controlled information sharing to better support both emotional burden and clinical coordination.
problem_solved: Family caregivers of people living with dementia often carry heavy emotional and practical responsibilities, but their own wellbeing is rarely tracked or supported within dementia care workflows. This paper addresses the gap between caregiver needs and clinician awareness/support.
method: Designed CareMirror, an envisioned caregiver wellbeing ecosystem with interconnected caregiver- and clinician-facing interfaces.
Used CareMirror as a design probe in semi-structured interviews with 14 caregivers to explore needs, barriers, and preferences.
Focused on longitudinal reflection, personalized support, and caregiver-controlled sharing with clinical care.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights how human-centered systems can extend beyond prediction to support longitudinal wellbeing, trust, and data-sharing control in sensitive healthcare settings. It also shows the importance of designing AI-enabled tools that respect caregiver agency and fit into real clinical ecosystems.
visual_elements: Two-panel ecosystem diagram showing caregiver app and clinician dashboard connected by shared signals
Journey timeline of caregiver wellbeing reflections over time
Flowchart of caregiver-controlled sharing from reflection to clinical care
Icon set for emotional load, support recommendations, privacy/control, and clinician feedback
paper_title: CareMirror: Bringing Caregiver Wellbeing into the Dementia Care Ecosystem
paper_authors: Jiayue Melissa Shi, Ethan Nguyen, Drishti Goel, Upasana Natarajan, Shashwat Srivatsa
